title: Normalized graph image as an intermediate valuation-curve model
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be normal $T$-curves with smooth generic fibres, let $f:Y\to X$ be an $\eta$-modification, and let $u:Y\to\mathbf P^1_T$ be any $T$-morphism [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $I$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $(f,u):Y\to\mathbf P^1_X$, namely the closed subscheme whose ideal is the kernel of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_X}\to(f,u)_*\mathcal O_Y$. Let $H$ be the normalization of $I$ in the product of the function fields of its components. Then $I$ is a reduced $T$-curve, $H\to I$ is finite, and $H$ is a normal $T$-curve. The graph map has a unique factorization $Y\xrightarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{g}X$, where both $q$ and $g$ are $\eta$-modifications and $gq=f$. Every geometric fibre of $q$ is connected. A fibre component $A$ of $Y$ is contracted by $q$ if and only if both $f|_A$ and $u|_A$ have zero-dimensional image. The modification locus of $q$ consists exactly of points with positive-dimensional fibre. In particular, $q$ is an isomorphism over each open of $X$ on which $f$ is an isomorphism. A component is contracted when its image has dimension zero; all assertions refer to the reduced underlying components. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A geometric fibre is the base change of a fibre to an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; geometrically reduced means all such fibres have no nonzero nilpotents. An $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism over the generic fibre and over schematically dense open subschemes; schematic density means injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ for the open inclusion. A scheme is normal if every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Its normalization means the scheme obtained by taking the integral closure of its structure sheaf in the product of the function fields of its irreducible components; for an integral scheme this is [def-sc-normalization].
